Risk call: refuse. This is the most concentrated pattern in the brief. Top-5 buyers hold 99.7% of early buy volume, bundle share is 1.0 and top-3 share is 1.0, and the first two minutes saw 644 SOL from only 19 external buyers. That's operator-backed at its most extreme, and even the break-even base rate assumes a far more dispersed holder set. The last 15 minutes show sellers (29) nearly matching buyers (31) with net outflow, and sell-to-buy in the launch window is 0.0012, which tells us the operator controls exit timing.

Pool depth of 739 SOL is ample for a $20 ticket, so liquidity isn't the constraint. The constraint is that any fill would be exit liquidity for a wallet cluster that can unload at will. A $20 position would lose 1.4-5.1% to fees on the round trip alone, before any move.

Sizing if the desk overrode: $5 minimum, 20% stop, 15-minute hold. But I would not buy. Skip it.

That reads as a single operator's position, not organic demand. The sell-to-buy ratio of 0.0012 in those first minutes is consistent with the operator accumulating rather than retail trading.

The last 15 minutes are the most recent signal: 10.43 SOL bought, 11.0 SOL sold, net flow of -0.57 SOL, 29 sellers against 31 buyers, and a -0.19% return. Demand is roughly flat to leaking, with distribution already visible. The 30-minute return of +5.9% and the small 0.38% drawdown are too thin to outweigh the concentration.

Against the base rates, an operator-class coin has been about break-even, and our $20 ticket would pay 1.4-5.1% in round-trip costs before any move. Nothing here says real demand will persist for 30-60 minutes. Skip.
